question: Two trains having lengths 550 m and 650 m are running parallel to each other in opposite directions at speeds of 68 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. In how much time (in seconds) they will cross each other?
solution:
**Given:**

L₁ = 550 m, S₁ = 68 km/h

L₂ = 650 m, S₂ = 40 km/h

**Calculation:**

⇒ S₁' = 68 × (1000/3600) = 18.89 m/s

⇒ S₂' = 40 × (1000/3600) = 11.11 m/s

Calculate the relative speed (S) and total distance (D):

⇒ S = S₁' + S₂' = 18.89 m/s + 11.11 m/s = 30 m/s

⇒ D = L₁ + L₂ = 550 m + 650 m = 1200 m

Calculate the time (T) using T = D/S:

⇒ T = D / S = 1200 m / 30 m/s = 40 seconds

**Hence, the trains will cross each other in 40 seconds**
